newsitem.title: USA: Bay View sees dilution from America First.
newsitem.headline: Bay View sees dilution from America First.

text.p: Bay View Capital Corp, which plans to aquire a unit of America First Financial Fund 1987-A Limited Partnership, forecast 1998 earnings dilution on an accounting basis of about $0.37 per share.

The purchase would be accretive on an accounting basis by about $0.19 per share in 1999, the company said. It said it executed a definitive pact to buy America First unit America First Eureka Holdings Inc. Under terms of the pact, America First Financial Fund would receive $300 million comprised of $210 million in Bay View stock and $90 million in cash.
The company also said because the acquisition would create a low-cost funding platform, Bay View would immediately cease its auto securitization operations.

This would reduce its 1997 net income by an estimated $2.9 million or $0.44 per share, it said. Net income for the second quarter would be reduced by about $1.0 million or $0.15 per share, it said. Earnings in 1998 and beyond would not be affected, the company said.

"We believe this decision will allow us to more effectively utilize the resulting funding platform at BVB," Bay View Chief Executive Edward Sondker said. "For 1998 and beyond, we believe this decision will further enhance our fianncial performance.

Bay View said it expected to record restructuring charges in 1997 associated with the deal of about $5 million pre-tax or about $2.9 million or $0.44 per share after tax. These charges were mostly for severance, facilities, relocation and debt restructuring costs related to the deal, it said.
Bay View was acquiring America First Eureka Holdings Inc and its wholly-owned subsidiary EurekaBank.

On a cash basis, Bay View said it expected the acquisition to enhance earnings by about $0.14 per share in 1998 and by about $0.74 in 1999. This excluded the amortization of goodwill arising from the deal, Bay View said.

"The accounting basis earnings per share will grow as we utilize this low-cost funding platform to domicile assets created from BVCC's rapidly expanding consumer and commercial finance platforms," Bay View Chief Financial Officer David Heaberlin said.
The acquisition would be accounted for as a purchase and was expected to be completed on or about December 31 or January 1, the company said.
Eureka would be merged into Bay View Bank and all EurekaBank branches would operate as Bay View Bank branches, the company said.
